content: For patients with type 1 diabetes, the administration of basal insulin alone is typically insufficient because these individuals are entirely dependent on exogenous insulin for survival. Even during periods of fasting, they often require a combination of basal insulin and prandial (mealtime) insulin to prevent the development of hyperglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis. Hospital protocols must include provisions to ensure the delivery of basal insulin, either through injection or continuous infusion, for patients with type 1 diabetes. Additionally, these protocols should account for adjustments in insulin therapy to accommodate changing requirements during transitions in care settings.
